strategy_name: Magic Formula: two-factor rank on quality (ROC) + value (earnings yield)
setup_summary: Rank the tradable universe by (a) EBIT / tangible capital employed (return on capital) and (b) EBIT / enterprise value (earnings yield), sum the two ranks, and buy the ~30 highest combined-rank names, holding each one year and rebalancing annually. On 17 years of US data (Compustat Point-in-Time, controlling for look-ahead/survivorship bias) the top-ranked ~30-stock portfolio returned ~30.8%/yr vs 12.3% for the equal-weighted market; decile analysis shows monotonic returns from Group 1 (17.9%/yr) to Group 10 (2.5%/yr). Perp analog (only if V8 expands beyond single-instrument): rank perp instruments by a quality proxy and a carry/value proxy (e.g., funding-adjusted yield normalized to notional), select the top-ranked basket, hold on a long cycle.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: rebalance at a fixed calendar interval (annually in the study); entry when an instrument is in the top combined-rank group. Invalidation: the thesis fails if the top-ranked decile stops beating the bottom-ranked decile over multi-year frozen OOS, or if crowding pushes ranked bargains to fair value so the rank spread collapses.
risk_geometry: Entry at market on the screen date; no price stop (margin of safety is the buffer); target is reversion toward fair value; exit after a fixed ~1-year hold (time stop / scheduled rebalance); risk is controlled by holding 20-30 names (diversification) rather than by per-name stops.
quote: Rather, the formula looks for the companies that have the best combination of those two factors.
chapter_anchor: Ch.6 p.54 (also Ch.6 p.51-52, Table 6.1; Ch.7 Table 7.2; Appendix p.139-144)
notes: Cross-sectional ranking across multiple perps is a ranker, which V8 keeps ABSENT by default (rule 6) - so this enters only as a registry experiment beating a simple baseline on frozen OOS. Requires a multi-instrument derivatives tape with funding (DATA_BLOCKED today, same gate as breakout_retest/capitulation). The earnings-yield-vs-risk-free-hurdle idea (buy only when yield exceeds ~6%) is part of the same ranking mechanism.
book: The Little Book That Beats the Market 2006

strategy_name: Graham net-net basket: buy assets priced below net liquidation value
setup_summary: Buy a basket of 20-30 names whose market price is below the proceeds of a fire-sale liquidation of the business's net current assets (Graham's 'bargain issues'). The book reports Graham used the formula successfully for 30+ years, that results were satisfactory with no further analysis, and that few if any stocks qualify today.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: any name trades below its estimated net liquidation value. Invalidation: the basket stops reverting to (or above) liquidation value over long horizons; in practice the current market rarely offers qualifying assets, which is itself an invalidation of the screen's capacity.
risk_geometry: Entry at market; no price stop; target = reversion toward asset value; long/no fixed expiry but effectively multi-year; risk controlled by holding a basket so individual names can fail.
quote: the purchase price was actually lower than the proceeds that would be received from simply shutting down the business and selling off the company's assets in a fire sale
notes: No book-value/liquidation-value analog exists for a token; the nearest crypto equivalent is a realized-cost/floor feature that is not part of this book. Keep as a gated backlog idea only if a realized-cost flow family is ever built; the transferable core is 'buy below a hard asset-backed floor and hold a diversified basket'.
book: The Little Book That Beats the Market 2006

strategy_name: Moat persistence: high return on capital signals a durable advantage and reinvestment-driven growth
setup_summary: A company that earns a high return on capital even for one year likely has a temporary special advantage (new concept/product, brand, network position) that keeps competition from eroding profits; such firms can reinvest profits at high rates, driving earnings growth (the Jason Gum Shops example: 50% ROC reinvested lifts earnings 50%/yr). Competition grinds ROC down toward average over time, so high ROC is a persistence signal, not a permanent state.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: prefer assets whose 'capital employed' earns a high return as a quality screen. Invalidation: ROC mean-reverts faster than expected (competitive entry), or the high-ROC year was a one-off that does not persist - the book itself concedes mediocre businesses can have a good year or two.
risk_geometry: n/a beyond the composite value strategy - this is the quality pillar's causal claim.
quote: In short, companies that achieve a high return on capital are likely to have a special advantage of some kind. That special advantage keeps competitors from destroying the ability to earn above-average profits.
notes: Kept separate from the composite two-factor finding because it is an independently falsifiable claim (ROC persistence / moat). There is no 'capital employed' for a token in the behavior-only stack; only usable as a cross-instrument quality filter if network-level fundamental data (revenue, active users, fees) is ever added. No short side exists in this book.
book: The Little Book That Beats the Market 2006

strategy_name: Open interest extremes at major turns
mechanism: Major tops/bottoms occur when open interest is the highest within a specific period (crowd fully committed); but OI alone is backward-looking and, in futures, polluted by contract-roll cycles
setup_summary: Track open interest relative to its recent range: major tops and bottoms tend to occur when OI is at its highest within a specific period, coinciding with Composite COT extremes. The book is skeptical of OI as a real-time trend-strength gauge ('increasing OI + increasing price = strong bull market' is backward looking) and notes FX futures OI tops recur on a 3-month contract cycle (March/June/Sept/Dec expiries), making mid-trend readings noisy.
trigger_invalidation: OI extremes alone do not time turns; the 3-month roll cycle produces false OI tops in futures. Requires confluence with positioning extremes (COT) or price structure.
quote: major tops and bottoms do tend to occur when open interest is its highest within a specific period. In this sense, open interest is valuable at the same time as the Composite COT.
notes: Crypto perp OI is continuous (no roll cycle), real-time, and OI-at-highs plus positive funding is a standard crowding read. Testable flow features: OI percentile over window, and the SSI-derived claim 'rising price + falling net positioning = short-covering rally (bearish)'.
book: Sentiment in the Forex Market - Indicators and Strategies To Profit from Crowd Behavior and Market Extremes 2008

strategy_name: Financial astrology / lunar-cycle timing (lunar buy-sell strategy)
mechanism: No causal price mechanism; claims that market cycles correlate with planetary/lunar cycles - lunations, new/full moon, Sun-Moon aspects, transits, and first-trade horoscopes - used to pick timing windows.
setup_summary: The book's central thesis: time entries around lunar/planetary cycles - e.g., a 'lunar buy-sell strategy' keyed to lunations (new moon = Sun/Moon conjunction, full moon = 180-degree opposition), transits, and Sun-Moon aspects (index: 'lunar buy-sell strategy', 'lunar cycles', 'choosing best trading periods').
trigger_invalidation: Not applicable - finding rejected for V8.
chapter_anchor: Glossary: lunation, new moon, full moon, transit, eclipse, aspect; Index: lunar buy-sell strategy, lunar cycles, financial astrology, Sun-Moon aspects
notes: No falsifiable causal mechanism; lunar phases are deterministic calendar data, but the book offers no statistical case (RBS 'Sheer Lunacy' skeptical paper is cited in the bibliography). V8 rejects as an autonomous expert; if ever examined, only as a pure calendar-correlation study under the astrology-for-timing framing, which V8's determinism rules do not preclude but the complexity budget does not justify.
book: Timing Solutions for Swing Traders - Successful Trading Using Technical Analysis and Financial Astrology 2012

mechanism: Extreme valuation (CAPE) implies lower forward expected returns; a slow valuation filter can time equity exposure.
setup_summary: When CAPE sits in an extreme/high band, reduce equity exposure or lengthen the risk-off state; the book covers this as an alternative timing approach to momentum timing.
risk_geometry: Slow filter; no stops; changes exposure at monthly+ cadence.
chapter_anchor: Index - 'Market timing: using valuation'; 'Shiller 10-year Cyclically Adjusted Price Earnings (CAPE) ratio, 123-124'
notes: Crypto perps have no earnings/CAPE analog; on-chain valuation (e.g., MVRV or unrealized-profit ratios) is outside this book's scope. Keep as a def-erred regime-filter idea; not implementable from this source. Only the index entry was auditable in Part 2.
book: Dual Momentum Investing - An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk 2015

strategy_name: Buy strength, sell weakness within a correlated group
setup_summary: When correlated markets signal simultaneously, take longs only in the strongest markets and shorts only in the weakest markets within the group, and enter only one unit per contract month. Strength measures: how many N price has advanced since breakout, or (price 3 months ago -> current price)/N, normalized across markets; the strongest group member almost always outperforms the rest to the long side, the weakest to the short side.
trigger_invalidation: Selection applies at signal time; a chosen instrument is invalidated if its own breakout stop/exit fires.
risk_geometry: Entry: breakout entry in the selected strongest/weakest instrument; same 2N stops and channel exits per instrument.
quote: If the signals came all at once, we always bought the strongest markets and sold short the weakest markets in a group... The strongest markets had the highest values; the weakest markets had the lowest.
chapter_anchor: Bonus Chapter 'Original Turtle Trading Rules', 'Buy Strength, Sell Weakness', pp. 271-272
notes: Not executable as-is in V8 (single-instrument BTCUSDT), but a strong candidate cross_market selection rule if the program expands to alt perps, where BTC/ETH/major correlations and funding divergence make leg selection material. Also a methodology caution: take only the one strongest/weakest leg rather than both sides of a correlated group.
book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

strategy_name: Covered call / collar family (synthetic short put)
mechanism: Covered calls and collars are options-market structures (long stock + short call; long put + short call) that synthesize option payoffs (synthetic short put) — they require an options or futures options market that V8's perp-underlying program does not have.
setup_summary: Rejected for V8: no perp-only expression of a covered call or collar exists on a plain BTCUSDT perpetual; the risk-perception lesson ('covered calls are much riskier than perceived — stock is not protected all the way down to zero') is worth keeping only as a general risk-education note, not as an executable family.
quote: Covered calls are much riskier then they are perceived to be because the stock is not protected all the way down to zero, only a portion of it.
chapter_anchor: Appendix, Final Exam Part II, Scenario 1 answers, p. 258; Scenario 3 (collar), p. 261
notes: Honest triage of the options-only chapters that bleed into Part 2's appendix scenarios (covered call, box, collar/reverse-collar). If V8 ever adds an options-data layer, the collar's 'skew makes reverse-collars near-credit' observation would be re-evaluated; today it is REJECT_FOR_V8.
book: Option Spread Strategies - Trading Up, Down, and Sideways Markets 2009

strategy_name: Market Breadth Divergence (AD-Line and Percent Above 200-Day)
mechanism: Index gains driven by fewer and fewer constituents are fragile: when the cumulative advance/decline line or the percent of assets above their 200-day average fails to confirm a new index high, breadth is diverging negatively and the rally is on weak footing, leading major indexes down at tops.
setup_summary: Track breadth over the asset universe: a cumulative advance-decline line and/or the percent of assets trading above their 200-period average (crypto analog of the NYSE % above 200-day). Healthy = index and breadth rise together. Warnings: index makes a new high while breadth fails (negative divergence); % above 200-day exceeds 70-85% (overextended) then breaks below 70%; a drop below 40% signals a bear regime (first such break in 4+ years was significant in 2007), and only a recovery above 60% signals a new bull. Breadth turns down before major indexes, especially at tops, because cap-weighted indexes hide widespread weakness.
trigger_invalidation: Breadth re-confirms (both lines rising together) → uptrend healthy; a rebound setup appears only when readings drop below 30% and then turn up.
risk_geometry: A filter/early-exit tool rather than an entry; the book uses it to take profits or defensive action ahead of the index decline; no stops/targets stated.
quote: While the NYSE was hitting a new high, only two-thirds of its stocks were still in uptrends.
chapter_anchor: Ch.8 'Market Breadth', 'Percent of NYSE Stocks Above 200-Day Average', 'NYSE Bullish Percent Index' (pp.163-182)
notes: Directly computable on crypto: percent of the top-N liquid coins above their 200-day MA is a widely used altcoin-regime indicator; advance-decline over the same universe is computable from index data. Belongs in participation/cross_market feature groups and can gate broad-market regime for V8.
book: The Visual Investor - How to Spot Market Trends 2nd edition 2009

strategy_name: Electronic front-running via fragmented order flow (signal leakage)
mechanism: Large-order intent leaks when an order is split across multiple venues; fast participants detect the first arrival and trade ahead on the remaining venues, moving price against the sender.
setup_summary: A large order is fragmented and routed to several venues at once. The first venue to receive it (e.g., BATS, physically closest) fills ~100% of displayed size while aggregated multi-venue fill collapses to a fraction; the price pops/plunges within milliseconds of entry as fast traders buy/sell ahead of the order on the other venues. Falsifiable on any timestamped multi-venue tape: fill rate falls as venue count rises, and the first venue's fills are systematically fuller (Brad observed 100% fills on BATS regardless of how many other exchanges he sent to).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: large order entry into a fragmented, thin market. Thesis (fragmentation leaks intent) is invalidated if simultaneous-arrival orders still produce partial fills and adverse price moves - which the book shows is NOT the case (synchronized arrival restored full fills).
risk_geometry: No entry/stop/target stated; this is an adverse-selection (implementation shortfall) mechanism, not a directional setup. For V8: relevant as a flow/participation feature (aggressive-order footprint, fill-quality warning) rather than an entry rule.
quote: some other trader was, in effect, noticing his demand for stock on one exchange and buying it on others in anticipation of selling it to him at a higher price
chapter_anchor: Chapter 2 (Brad's Problem) - the AMD/Intel live demo and Thor discovery
notes: Victim-side lesson of the book's central mechanism. In crypto, a single dominant venue (Binance) removes 13-venue fragmentation arbitrage, but large-order footprint is still observable in the trade print and cross-exchange/index latency games exist; the transferable V8 seed is a large-aggressive-order feature. The predator-side detection vehicle (resting 100-share sentinel orders on BATS used 'to tease information out of investors'; latency tables used to fingerprint brokers) is a distinct flow-intelligence tactic that is DATA_BLOCKED for a bar-level tape - flagged in this finding rather than emitted as a separate expert.
book: Flash Boys - A Wall Street Revolt 2015

mechanism: cheapness relative to recent history is not a reversal trigger; in a structurally deteriorating asset one problem surfaces after another, eroding any initial discount
setup_summary: Standing rule: an entry triggered mainly by 'price is cheap vs its own recent range/history' (deep drawdown from highs, oversold oscillator, large discount to a slow anchor) is rejected unless an independent structural-reversal condition is present. Perp crypto analog: structurally declining assets (persistent lower highs, net outflows, weakening funding) that look 'cheap' keep printing lower lows.
trigger_invalidation: N/A (standing rule). A long is only admitted with a separate reversal thesis (e.g., forced-selling exhaustion), never on cheapness alone.
risk_geometry: Entry refused on cheapness-only signal; if admitted via another thesis, stop at structure, modest R target, short expiry.
quote: In a difficult business, no sooner is one problem solved than another surfaces—never is there just one cockroach in the kitchen.
chapter_anchor: Part II.F Cigar Butts and the Institutional Imperative (1989), pp. 93-95
notes: Crypto is full of chronically 'cheap' assets that keep declining (structural dilution, fading usage). Guards the capitulation family: only exhaustion, not cheapness, is the trigger. SHORT-side implication: persistent structural decline is a valid short thesis even when the asset 'looks cheap'.
book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

strategy_name: Limit-order adverse selection: backtests overstate fills on resting orders
mechanism: a resting limit order fills only when the book on the other side at that price is consumed - which is precisely when price is moving through your level against you; it is missed when price would have come back, so real fills are winners-missed/losers-caught
setup_summary: Any strategy that enters on limit orders, or exits via limit profit-targets, will realize worse fills than a fill-guaranteed backtest: the book's emini-S&P 5-minute scalp backtested at $15.90/trade with a straight-line equity curve (928 wins/330 losses), and in live auto-trading 'just about all of the losing trades would occur, but you'd only get about half the winners.'
trigger_invalidation: Not a market rule; a fill-modeling rule. Its scope is any V8 candidate whose risk_geometry uses limit entries or limit profit-targets.
risk_geometry: Simulator-side: penalize limit-order fills with an adverse-selection model (fill probability that depends on which way price is moving through the level), and scale the penalty inversely with profit-per-trade - small-profit scalps are killed, large-profit systems merely degrade.
quote: I missed some of the best fills, but always got filled on the ones that traded down to my price, and kept going down from there. In other words, I missed some big winners, but always seemed to get the losers.
notes: V8's canonical L1 simulator is fill-at-close with STOP_FIRST - it currently has no representation of limit-order fill bias. For perps, maker orders are the cost-efficient execution (rebates), so any future candidate using maker entries inherits this exact bias, amplified by leverage. Also relevant: the book's dual-orders-in-a-bar and assuming-every-point-in-a-bar-is-a-trade-point warnings argue for keeping V8's fill-at-close L1 rather than intra-bar path assumptions.
book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

strategy_name: Margin of Safety (large discount between price and estimated value)
mechanism: a dramatic gap between price and a conservatively estimated value absorbs miscalculation and worse-than-average luck; the asymmetry protects the buyer over time
setup_summary: Act only when price sits at a large discount to a conservatively estimated value: Buffett estimates an asset at X to 3X and attempts to buy at 1/2X ('the gap should be dramatic, not a dollar of value for 97 cents'). Translated to a perp trade: require a minimum reward:risk asymmetry (target R clearly above stop R, ideally >=2:1) so the position survives miscalculation, and reject any entry where price is near the thesis value.
trigger_invalidation: Thesis is invalid if the estimated value itself falls (the underlying business/catalyst deteriorates) rather than the discount merely closing; a discount that only closes because price rises toward value is a win, not an invalidation.
risk_geometry: Entry at a large discount to a frozen estimate of value; the margin itself is the protection (no stop specified by the book); requires target R > stop R with a minimum asymmetry buffer.
quote: When you build a bridge, you insist it can carry 30,000 pounds, but you only drive 10,000-pound trucks across it.
chapter_anchor: 1986 'Value Investing' section; 1989 'Intrinsic Business Value (IBV)' ('if he and Munger get a value of X to 3X for an asset, then they attempt to buy it at 1/2X')
notes: BTCUSDT has no fundamental cash-flow value, so the transferable core is the asymmetry gate: require reward:risk >1:1 in risk_geometry so miscalculation is survivable. Current V8 experts use target_r 1.0 / stop_r 1.0; this argues for a required asymmetry floor on formalized experts.
book: University of Berkshire Hathaway - 30 Years of Lessons Learned from Warren Buffett & Charlie Munger at the Annual Shareholders Meeting 2017

setup_summary: Lifecycle rule: do not trade perp instruments with insufficient listing history - the party that creates/lists the instrument chooses the timing, so early history carries adverse-selection and supply-overhang risk ('the insiders are selling their company'). Concretely: a perp is eligible only after a minimum bar history supports a credible sample and liquidity.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: candidate on an instrument younger than the minimum listing age. Invalidation: instrument becomes eligible when history/liquidity thresholds are met.
quote: Avoid new issues—the insiders are selling their company, so it's ridiculous to think that an IPO will be the cheapest thing to buy in a world of thousands of stocks.
notes: Applies if the V8 universe expands beyond BTCUSDT to alt perps; trivially satisfied for BTC itself. Maps to a listing-age gate in lifecycle.
book: University of Berkshire Hathaway - 30 Years of Lessons Learned from Warren Buffett & Charlie Munger at the Annual Shareholders Meeting 2017

strategy_name: Monetary-regime valuation anchor (interest rates as gravity)
setup_summary: Regime filter: broad rate/liquidity conditions are the gravity that sets the level of all asset prices - near-zero rates and liquidity pumping buoy risk assets regardless of micro structure, and the market reprices when the regime turns (the impact lands 'when the market senses the Fed has changed course'). For BTCUSDT: gate long-bias risk on a cross_market monetary-regime feature (rates, DXY, liquidity) rather than treating each 1h setup in isolation.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: candidate episodes assessed against the prevailing monetary-regime feature. Invalidation: regime flip (rates rising / liquidity turning) downgrades long setups and upgrades repricing risk.
quote: Interest rates are to asset prices sort of like gravity is to the apple.
chapter_anchor: 2013 annual meeting, 'Effects of ZBIR'; 2015 'Stock Market and Interest Rates' (market cap to GDP at 125%, corporate profits to GDP >10%)
notes: Needs cross_market data (rates/DXY/liquidity) that the current frozen spec does not carry; the total-marketcap-to-GDP / profit-share screens are the BTC MVRV-analog valuation check. DEFER_GATED until data exists.
